notes: Element X is the Matrix messenger on Google Play (io.element.android.x, 500k+ installs), designed against Element's Compound design system by an in-house design team. It has the largest preview corpus of anything surveyed: 494 preview-bearing files, of which 116 are in :libraries:designsystem alone — the buttons, dialogs, list items and avatars, each one screenshot-tested, which is what makes them self-contained enough to render outside the app. Ordinary Android Compose in src/main/kotlin, so the Robolectric lane. ref is develop, which is this project's default branch. previewAnnotations names PreviewsDayNight, the day/night multipreview the module's own previews carry: it is declared in this same module so the source pre-flight would probably see it, but naming it costs nothing and the failure it prevents ('matches no @Preview function in the scanned module') is opaque. Licence: AGPL-3.0 — see the note on the pull request. The render still fails, and the one hypothesis on the table is now disproven. All 321 previews in :libraries:designsystem die at class-init with ClassNotFoundException on androidx.customview.poolingcontainer.R$id, thrown from PoolingContainer.kt:121 — so the ARTIFACT is on the classpath and executing, and only its AGP-generated R class is missing. The plugin already pins that artifact onto the main variant for exactly this reason and manageDependencies is on, so the pin applies and is not enough. Ruled out by evidence rather than argument: android.nonTransitiveRClass=false, which makes AGP generate dependency R classes into the consumer's R.jar, was carried through gradleProperties in run 79 (the step reports success, so the property was written into the throwaway checkout) and the failure is byte-for-byte the same — it is removed here rather than left in place as a guess nobody revisited. Also ruled out: product flavors (this is a plain library) and any upstream exclusion of the group; msasikanth-twine sets nonTransitiveRClass and publishes fine. It cannot be reproduced locally because element-x resolves matrix-analytics-events from jitpack.io, which the sandbox blocks. Tracked in compose-ai-tools#5026.
